For extrs. an. discussion see JASB. 65 (1896) p.. 20. 29.

Ghaṭakarpara
one of the nine gems in the court of King Vikramāditya according to a tradition recorded in Jyotirvidābharaṇa; also given a. the name of the poem.
--Ghaṭakarparakāvya. See below. [Page267-a.
--Nītisāra. ascribed. See Keith, HSL. p.. 200-1.
Pt.. Kāvyasaṅgraha Pt. I. p.. 374-380. Jīvānandavidyāsāgar. Calcutta, 1888.

Ghaṭakarpara
yamaka kāvya in 22 verses in different metres expressing the feelings of a lady whose husband is away (Proṣitapatikā) a. the beg. of the rainy season; the name used for the poem an. often for its a. is due to the reference to ‘a potsherd (ghaṭakarpara)’ in a wager in its last verse; ascribed to Ghaṭakarpara, one of the nine gems of Vikramāditya's court according to tradition; many mss. an. commentaries ascribe it to Kālidāsa.
See V. Raghavan, Mirashi Fel. Vol. (Nagpur) 1965. p.. 148-9.
On the Ghaṭakarpara an. the Meghadūta see C.. Vaudville, Proceed. AIOC. Vol. 20, Pt. II. i. p.. 37-48; J. B. Chaudhuri (Intro. to his edn.) considers Gh. earlier than Meghadūta an. a. representing a. intermediate stage between the epic an. Meghadūta.
On the different titles of the poem, Ghaṭakarpara, Gh. kalāpakāvya, Gh. kulaka, Gh. kāvya, its authorship an. its literary value, see K. C. Pandey, Abhinavagupta (2nd edn. 1963) p.. 94-131.
Kṛṣṇalīlā of Madana is a Samasyāpūraṇakāvya using lines from Ghaṭakarpara. See NCC. IV. p. 353.
See also S. L. Katre, ‘The Ghaṭakarpara problem’. Vikrama Volume, Ujjain, p.. 177-198.
